note: E1; E10: FY2023 highlights record zero cases of regulatory breaches and non-compliance, data security breaches, and corruption and fraud; E10 confirms zero non-compliance incidents in FY2023. E4 performance table is truncated before its performance column, so it is not relied on.

E11-E12: the 2022 report still has no target set and defers disclosure of the target to the next sustainability report, a moved deadline; the 2021 (deadline-year) evidence shows no quantitative energy target, only renewable-energy plans and index entries (E2, E8-E9). Caveat: E11 speaks of an emissions target, which LHN reports within its energy consumption section (E8); if read as a different target this would be unclear.

E7; E9: FY2024 reports 14,261.9 MWh of renewable energy across the Australia and UK properties, up about 6% on FY2023, but gives no share of total energy purchased and no verdict on the 70% target. E1 performance table is truncated before this target; E13 (2025) sets a new 100% target without a FY2024 result.

E6: 2023 water consumption intensity is 1.45 t/t steam sold, but no 2022 figure is in the evidence to check the 1% reduction. E12's 'target has been achieved' refers to the 2024 target against 2023, not this one; E13 is the 2024 figure.

E5-E6: zero substantiated complaints concerning breaches of customer privacy in FY2024, in the same passage that renews the target for FY2025; the company reports this GRI 418-1 complaint count as its measure for the zero-incident target (E2). Wording is complaints rather than incidents, leaks or thefts.
E11: the 2023 report lists Ang Mo Kio among the sites where the LMS is available.
E1; E3: FY2024 return on equity recorded 25.9%, target marked achieved; E10 shows FY2025 also met.

E6-E7: zero substantiated complaints concerning breaches of customer privacy in FY2021, directly followed by the renewed target for FY2022; the company reports the GRI 418-1 complaint count as its measure for this target. E8-E10 (2022 report) repeat the FY2021 result.

E3-E15: the FY2024 and FY2025 evidence covers new sustainability targets, IFRS S1/S2 gap assessment, stakeholder engagement and the materiality review; nothing refers to formalising policies and procedures (P&P) for key business activities.

E4-E5: in 2024 an additional mill, the Komering sugar factory, was audited as part of ISO 50001 certification preparation, with further audits planned for 2025; the qualitative aim of more mills audited in 2024 is met, though only one more mill and no palm oil mill. E2/E8-E11 ISPO/PROPER coverage is a different audit.

E8: the flattened 'Towards 2025 and Beyond' table shows '25 role models in the field of sport' between the 2021 and 2022-2025 column headers, so it cannot be read as the 2021 result; E7 is general; E10 (2022) sets a 20-per-year target. No clear 2021 count against the 24 players.

E4-E6: in 2023 solar rooftops were installed at two distribution centers (Nakhon Ratchasima and Surat Thani) and by HAVI at Bangplee in Samut Prakan (not described as a distribution center); Ayutthaya is not reported, and the 2024 plan moves to Chon Buri and Pathum Thani. The stated 2023 figure (two DCs) falls short of the four named sites.
E3: no reported substantiated complaints concerning breaches of data privacy and losses of personal data in FY2023 (FY2022: nil); E11 shows the same target met again in FY2024.

E6: the FY2022 performance table marks zero incidents of confirmed corruption and zero incidents of non-compliance with laws and regulations as 'Yes, all achieved'; E3 reports no non-compliance from FY2022 audits.
E2: FY2022 highlights record zero cases of corruption and fraud; E7-E8 performance-against-targets table for FY2022 repeats zero cases. E9 (2023) shows zero cases again.
